l: PICWiki, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 1 / Introduction
s: PICWiki is a knowledge corpus derived from Wikipedia that contains each document's original text, generated pseudo-instruction, and PIC-processed chunks. It is intended to serve as a text knowledge base for RAG without requiring model retraining.

l: WikiDump, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 1 / Introduction
s: The authors use the latest English WikiDump to process documents into chunks for a RAG knowledge base. The resulting chunks are evaluated through open-domain question-answering tasks.

l: open-domain question-answering benchmarks, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 1 / Introduction
s: Open-domain question-answering benchmarks are used to evaluate different chunking methods. PIC outperforms existing approaches on retrieval performance measured by Hits@k and end-to-end question-answering performance measured by Exact Match.

l: hallucinations, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 1 / Introduction
s: The unit describes hallucinations as a problem that Retrieval-Augmented Generation aims to mitigate. It states that irrelevant information in large chunks can interfere with retrieval and generation, leading to hallucinations.

l: Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / Related Works
s: This unit reviews Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) methods, emphasizing improvements to retrievers, generation reliability, and retrieval-unit design. It states that most prior RAG work overlooks chunk quality, while newer approaches use semantic relationships and large language models to improve document segmentation. The unit also presents a proposed method, PIC, which dynamically segments documents according to the similarity between sentences and a pseudo-instruction. The Chinese New Year example illustrates how documents about the Spring Festival can be divided into semantically related chunks.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / Related Works
s: Retrieval-Augmented Generation has been shown to be effective for knowledge-intensive NLP tasks. Existing methods mainly improve retriever performance, design the broader RAG pipeline, or enhance the reliability of language-model generation, but most overlook the impact of chunk quality on downstream performance.

l: retriever, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / Related Works
s: RAG research has improved retrievers through dense passage retrieval, reranking, multiple retrieval strategies, and knowledge-graph-based traversal. Retrievers select relevant units from a knowledge base based on user instructions.

l: chunk quality, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / Related Works
s: The unit identifies chunk quality as an important factor in downstream RAG performance that most existing methods overlook. It motivates improved chunking approaches that preserve semantic relationships within retrieval units.

l: retrieval units, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / Related Works
s: Retrieval units are smaller pieces into which long documents are split before storage in a knowledge base. They can occur at sentence, paragraph, or document granularity and may be created using fixed size, punctuation, phrase structure, or semantic relationships.

l: documents, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / Related Works
s: Documents are split into smaller retrieval units for storage and later retrieval in RAG systems. In the PIC illustration, a document about the Chinese New Year is dynamically segmented according to the similarity between its sentences and a pseudo-instruction.

l: semantic chunking, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / Related Works
s: Semantic chunking uses relationships between text segments to determine retrieval-unit boundaries. Described approaches compare adjacent-sentence embeddings, detect semantic transition points, or use perplexity to identify coherent chunk boundaries.

l: large language models, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / Related Works
s: Large language models are described as capturing semantic dependencies better than simpler methods. They are used to rewrite sentences into contextualized segments with restored pronouns and to detect semantic transition points for chunking.

l: Chinese New Year, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / Related Works
s: Chinese New Year is used as the topic in the PIC example. The associated documents discuss its historical origins, traditional customs, family reunions, cultural heritage, modern evolution, and impact on Chinese communities worldwide.

l: Spring Festival, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 2 / Related Works
s: Spring Festival is identified as the common Chinese name for Chinese New Year. The text states that the festival incorporates regional customs and traditions that vary widely within China.

l: Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 / Methodology .. 3.2 / Chunking Based on Pseudo-Instructions
s: This unit presents a methodology for chunking documents in the context of retrieval-augmented generation. It generates pseudo-instructions from a document summary and uses them to guide semantic chunking. Sentences are encoded and compared with the summary using cosine similarity, and adjacent sentences are grouped into relevant or irrelevant chunks according to a dynamic threshold. The threshold is set to the mean similarity between all sentences and the document summary.

l: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 / Methodology .. 3.2 / Chunking Based on Pseudo-Instructions
s: Retrieval-augmented generation requires an effective chunking strategy to support retrieval and generation performance.

l: chunking strategy, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 / Methodology .. 3.2 / Chunking Based on Pseudo-Instructions
s: The chunking strategy segments a document into semantically coherent chunks. It uses pseudo-instructions and semantic similarity to group adjacent sentences while minimizing unrelated information.

l: document D, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 / Methodology .. 3.2 / Chunking Based on Pseudo-Instructions
s: Document D consists of n sentences and is segmented into a set of m chunks. A summarizer generates a summary for document D, which is then used to guide chunking.

l: sentences, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 / Methodology .. 3.2 / Chunking Based on Pseudo-Instructions
s: Sentences in document D are encoded with an embedding model and compared individually with the document summary. Adjacent sentences with similarity scores on the same side of the threshold are grouped together.

l: chunks, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 / Methodology .. 3.2 / Chunking Based on Pseudo-Instructions
s: Chunks consist of one or more combined sentences. They are classified as relevant or irrelevant according to whether their sentences have similarity scores above or below the threshold.

l: pseudo-instructions, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 / Methodology .. 3.2 / Chunking Based on Pseudo-Instructions
s: Pseudo-instructions guide chunking without requiring knowledge of the real distribution of user instructions. In this methodology, document summaries serve as pseudo-instructions.

l: document summaries, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 / Methodology .. 3.2 / Chunking Based on Pseudo-Instructions
s: A summarizer generates a concise and informative summary for document D. The summary preserves key document information and provides the embedding used for sentence comparisons.

l: semantic similarity, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 / Methodology .. 3.2 / Chunking Based on Pseudo-Instructions
s: Semantic similarity is computed between each sentence and the document summary using cosine similarity between their embeddings. The resulting score determines whether adjacent sentences are grouped into relevant or irrelevant chunks.

l: similarity threshold, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 3 / Methodology .. 3.2 / Chunking Based on Pseudo-Instructions
s: The similarity threshold controls the chunking condition. It is dynamically set to the mean similarity between all sentences in document D and its summary, rather than being fixed across documents.

l: Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 4 / Experimental Settings .. 4.4 / Implementation Details
s: This unit evaluates document chunking methods for Retrieval-Augmented Generation using the 2024-12-01 English Wikipedia dump and six OpenQA benchmarks. It compares rule-based, semantic-based, generation-based, and PIC chunking methods through retrieval performance measured by Hits@k and end-to-end question-answering performance measured by Exact Match. PIC achieves the highest average retrieval performance, with 58.4 Top-5 and 69.5 Top-20 Hits@k, outperforming the listed baselines. The experiments use GPT-4o-mini for summarization, bge-en-large-v1.5 for embeddings and retrieval, and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct for answer generation.

l: experimental evaluation of document chunking methods, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 4 / Experimental Settings .. 4.4 / Implementation Details
s: The experimental evaluation compares document chunking methods in Retrieval-Augmented Generation scenarios using Wikipedia and six knowledge-intensive OpenQA tasks. It assesses retrieval and end-to-end question-answering performance with two different LLMs.

s: Retrieval-Augmented Generation is the application setting used to evaluate the chunking methods. Retrieved chunks are concatenated with input instructions before answer generation.

s: The OpenQA benchmarks used are Natural Questions, TriviaQA, WebQuestions, SQuAD, EntityQuestions, and PopQA. They evaluate reading comprehension and answering natural-language queries using Wikipedia or structured knowledge bases.

l: PIC, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 4 / Experimental Settings .. 4.4 / Implementation Details
s: PIC is evaluated alongside the baseline chunking methods and achieves the highest average retrieval performance in both Top-5 and Top-20 Hits@k. It records average scores of 58.4 Top-5 and 69.5 Top-20.

l: PICWiki, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 4 / Experimental Settings .. 4.4 / Implementation Details
s: PICWiki is the dataset produced by applying PIC to the same Wikipedia corpus. It is described as being suitable for plug-and-play integration into RAG systems, and the authors plan to release it.

l: rule-based chunking methods, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 4 / Experimental Settings .. 4.4 / Implementation Details
s: Rule-based chunking is evaluated through sentence-by-sentence, paragraph-by-paragraph, and fixed-size window segmentation. The fixed-size method creates 100-word chunks while preserving sentence boundaries.

l: semantic chunking, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 4 / Experimental Settings .. 4.4 / Implementation Details
s: Semantic-based chunking segments documents according to the semantic consistency of adjacent sentences. It uses sentence embeddings, computes adjacent-sentence similarity, and splits below the 20th-percentile similarity threshold.

l: generation-based chunking, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 4 / Experimental Settings .. 4.4 / Implementation Details
s: Generation-based chunking generates text chunks from documents. The evaluated approach rewrites sentences into self-contained atomic expressions called propositions.

l: Proposition, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 4 / Experimental Settings .. 4.4 / Implementation Details
s: Proposition is a generation-based chunking method associated with Chen et al. (2024). It first segments text into 100-word passages and uses the Propositionizer model to rewrite them into propositions.

s: GPT-4o-mini is used as the summarizer to generate summaries for all documents. The summarization uses a prompt provided in Appendix C.

s: Exact Match measures end-to-end question-answering performance as the percentage of questions for which the predicted answer exactly matches the ground truth.

s: Document chunking is evaluated through rule-based, semantic-based, generation-based, and PIC methods. The resulting chunks are used for retrieval and downstream question answering.

s: Retrieval performance is evaluated with Hits@5 and Hits@20 across six OpenQA benchmarks. PIC achieves the highest average retrieval scores among the listed methods.

s: End-to-end QA performance evaluates how chunking affects the question-answering abilities of the RAG system. It is measured with Exact Match using Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct.

s: Question answering is evaluated on six OpenQA benchmarks involving natural-language queries and knowledge from Wikipedia or structured knowledge bases. Retrieved chunks are supplied to an LLM that generates the answer.

l: Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / Main Results / 5.1 / Retrieval Performance .. 5.2 / End-to-end QA Performance
s: The unit evaluates PIC against sentence, paragraph, fixed-size, semantic, and proposition chunking methods on retrieval and end-to-end question-answering tasks across six datasets. PIC achieves the highest average retrieval performance and consistently produces the best QA results with both Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct. PIC performs less strongly on SQuAD, likely because its questions come from relatively few documents and resemble reading comprehension. QA accuracy is lower than retrieval accuracy overall, but PIC has the smallest performance drop, which the authors attribute to reduced irrelevant information in its chunks.

l: PIC, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / Main Results / 5.1 / Retrieval Performance .. 5.2 / End-to-end QA Performance
s: PIC achieves the highest average retrieval performance across six datasets and consistently obtains the best end-to-end QA results with both evaluated LLMs. Its retrieval performance is suboptimal on SQuAD, but it has the smallest drop from retrieval to QA performance, which the authors attribute to reduced irrelevant information and fewer hallucinations.

l: retrieval performance, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / Main Results / 5.1 / Retrieval Performance .. 5.2 / End-to-end QA Performance
s: Retrieval performance is highest on average for PIC across the six datasets, with the largest reported improvement on WebQ. The text notes that retrieval accuracy can exceed QA accuracy because retrieving relevant text does not always lead the LLM to produce the correct answer.

l: end-to-end QA performance, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / Main Results / 5.1 / Retrieval Performance .. 5.2 / End-to-end QA Performance
s: End-to-end question-answering performance is consistently best for PIC across experiments with two different LLMs. Compared with retrieval performance, QA performance is substantially lower, but PIC shows the smallest performance decline among the evaluated methods.

l: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / Main Results / 5.1 / Retrieval Performance .. 5.2 / End-to-end QA Performance
s: With Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct as the generation model, PIC achieves the best QA results, improving the average by 2 points across six datasets and by 5.7 points on EQ. Under the top-5 setting, PIC declines by 8.5 points from retrieval to QA performance, compared with larger declines for Proposition and Semantic chunking.

l: Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / Main Results / 5.1 / Retrieval Performance .. 5.2 / End-to-end QA Performance
s: With Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct as the generation model, PIC again achieves the best QA results and shows an average improvement of nearly 1 point.

l: document chunking, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 5 / Main Results / 5.1 / Retrieval Performance .. 5.2 / End-to-end QA Performance
s: The unit compares sentence, paragraph, fixed-size, semantic, proposition, and PIC chunking methods for retrieval and QA. The results suggest that chunking with less irrelevant information helps LLMs identify answers more effectively and reduces hallucinations.

l: Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 6 / Further Analysis / 6.1 / Impacts of the Pseudo-Instruction .. 6.4 / Chunk Analysis
s: This unit analyzes how pseudo-instruction design, chunking thresholds, and instruction-based chunking affect retrieval and question-answering performance. Using a document summary as the pseudo-instruction performs better than using a random summary, a random sentence, or the mean sentence embedding, while the mean similarity threshold gives the best results. Chunking with real instructions achieves the strongest results on NaturalQuestions and Qasper. Further analysis finds that chunk structure matters more than chunk length and that PIC retrieves a majority of relevant chunks across datasets.

l: pseudo-instructions, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 6 / Further Analysis / 6.1 / Impacts of the Pseudo-Instruction .. 6.4 / Chunk Analysis
s: The pseudo-instruction guides chunking so that segmented chunks better align with the possible real instruction distribution. Using a document's summary as the pseudo-instruction performs better than using a random summary, a random sentence, or the mean of sentence embeddings.

l: PIC, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 6 / Further Analysis / 6.1 / Impacts of the Pseudo-Instruction .. 6.4 / Chunk Analysis
s: PIC uses summaries as pseudo-instructions to organize document sentences into chunks according to their relevance to the document's central theme. It achieves the best retrieval and question-answering performance among the tested pseudo-instruction implementations and retrieves more than 50% relevant chunks in all evaluated datasets.

l: document chunking, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 6 / Further Analysis / 6.1 / Impacts of the Pseudo-Instruction .. 6.4 / Chunk Analysis
s: Document chunking is evaluated using pseudo-instructions and, when available, real instructions. The analysis concludes that the structure of the text within each chunk has a greater effect on downstream performance than chunk length itself.

l: document summaries, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 6 / Further Analysis / 6.1 / Impacts of the Pseudo-Instruction .. 6.4 / Chunk Analysis
s: A summary is used as the pseudo-instruction because it encapsulates the document's main information and supports segmentation based on relevance to the central theme. Summary-based pseudo-instructions outperform random summaries, randomly selected sentences, and mean sentence embeddings.

l: real instruction, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 6 / Further Analysis / 6.1 / Impacts of the Pseudo-Instruction .. 6.4 / Chunk Analysis
s: Real instructions are used for chunking when the actual user instruction distribution is known. Chunking with real instructions produces the best results in the reported experiments on NaturalQuestions and Qasper.

l: retrieval performance, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 6 / Further Analysis / 6.1 / Impacts of the Pseudo-Instruction .. 6.4 / Chunk Analysis
s: Retrieval performance is highest when summaries are used as pseudo-instructions and when the chunking threshold is set at the mean similarity. PIC retrieves relevant chunks as more than half of the retrieved chunks across all evaluated datasets.

l: end-to-end QA performance, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 6 / Further Analysis / 6.1 / Impacts of the Pseudo-Instruction .. 6.4 / Chunk Analysis
s: Question-answering performance follows the same general pattern as retrieval performance: summary-based PIC and a threshold at the mean produce the strongest results. Real-instruction chunking achieves the highest reported question-answering scores on NaturalQuestions and Qasper.

l: similarity threshold, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 6 / Further Analysis / 6.1 / Impacts of the Pseudo-Instruction .. 6.4 / Chunk Analysis
s: The chunking threshold is based on the mean similarity between sentences and the summary, with experiments ranging from the mean minus two standard deviations to the mean plus two standard deviations. The mean threshold performs best, while thresholds that are too high or too low mix relevant and irrelevant sentences more or reduce the method toward no chunking.

l: relevant chunks, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 6 / Further Analysis / 6.1 / Impacts of the Pseudo-Instruction .. 6.4 / Chunk Analysis
s: Relevant chunks are intended to contain more key information from a document and therefore be easier to retrieve. They constitute more than 50% of the retrieved PIC chunks across all reported datasets, and nearly all retrieved golden chunks on EQ and PopQA are relevant chunks.

l: Natural Questions, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 6 / Further Analysis / 6.1 / Impacts of the Pseudo-Instruction .. 6.4 / Chunk Analysis
s: NaturalQuestions is used with Qasper to evaluate real-instruction chunking. It consists of real anonymized queries issued to the Google search engine paired with corresponding Wikipedia pages, and real-instruction chunking achieves a QA score of 39.2 compared with 38.8 for PIC.

l: Qasper, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 6 / Further Analysis / 6.1 / Impacts of the Pseudo-Instruction .. 6.4 / Chunk Analysis
s: Qasper is used with NaturalQuestions to evaluate real-instruction chunking. It contains human-written question-answer pairs based on NLP papers, and real-instruction chunking achieves an F1 score of 16.2 compared with 15.6 for PIC.

l: Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Document Segmentation Matters for Retrieval-Augmented Generation, 7 / Conclusions / Limitations
s: The paper identifies document segmentation as a critical but underexplored challenge in retrieval-augmented generation systems. It proposes PIC, a document chunking method that uses document summaries as pseudo-instructions to guide semantic chunking and group sentences by relevance to the document topic. Across six QA benchmarks, PIC improves retrieval accuracy and end-to-end QA performance without additional model retraining. The paper notes computational overhead from summary generation and limits its evaluation to general-domain tasks, leaving cross-document reasoning for future work.

l: SafeRAG: Benchmarking Security in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, SafeRAG: Benchmarking Security in Retrieval-Augmented Generation, SafeRAG: Benchmarking Security in Retrieval-Augmented Generation / Abstract
s: SafeRAG is a benchmark introduced by Xun Liang, Simin Niu, Zhiyu Li, Sensen Zhang, Hanyu Wang, Feiyu Xiong, Jason Zhaoxin Fan, Bo Tang, Jihao Zhao, Jiawei Yang, Shichao Song, and Mengwei Wang to evaluate security in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). The authors classify RAG attack tasks into silver noise, inter-context conflict, soft ad, and white Denial-of-Service, and construct the SafeRAG dataset primarily manually for these tasks. Experiments on 14 representative RAG components show significant vulnerability to all four attack tasks, which can bypass existing retrievers, filters, or advanced large language models and degrade RAG service quality.
